unlisted_practices: Design AI mental health applications as therapist-AI partnerships that augment therapy while addressing the need for authentic human empathy, compassion, and care when relevant for treatment success.
Do not use conversational AI as a quick-fix solution at all times in mental health contexts, since some patients need long-term human connection.
Plan AI mental health interventions to mitigate the risk of long-term patient overdependency on the AI tool.

Evaluate empirically in future studies whether AI-generated responses can be experienced as empathic when users know their artificial origin, and how this relates to treatment outcomes by patients' theory of change.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/perspective paper examining the role of empathy in AI-driven therapy and outlining considerations for researchers and clinicians regarding when AI can replace humans versus when human connection is essential.
